sentences.text: First application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to repeat the prayer after examination of prosecutrix vide order dated 26.09.2022 in M.Cr.C. No. 6965/2022.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.177/2022, registered at Police Station - Kondagaon, District - Kondagaon (C.G.) for offence punishable under section 376 (2) (n), 376 (3)
of Indian Penal Code, 1860, section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: 2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the applicant committed sexual intercourse with the minor prosecutrix on several occasion on false pretext of marriage due to which she got pregnant.
3. Mr. Shobhit Koshta learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has not committed the aforesaid crime and has been falsely implicated.

It is submitted that prosecutrix is examined before the learned trial court and her statement does not inspire Umesh Rathore vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71372795/
1 confidence.

sentences.text: He further submits that in the cross examination, the prosecutrix has at stated that she got pregnant from some one else.
Therefore she is not a credible witness and she cannot be termed as sterling witness.
She appears to be major and consenting party.
The applicant is in jail from 06.05.2022 and trial is likely to take some time.
Therefore the application may be allowed and the applicant may be released on regular bail.

4. Refuting to the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, Ms. Madhunisha Singh Deputy Advocate General for the non-applicant/state vehemently argued that from the evidence collected by the prosecution case is made out against the applicant.

She further submits that from the statement of the prosecutrix it is aptly clear that the applicant committed sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix with false pretext of marriage and her consent was obtained by fraud and misconception of fact hence it cannot be said that the prosecutrix was a consenting party.
She submits that the prosecutrix is less than 18 years hence her consent is immaterial.
Even otherwise the factum of consent can be determined at the time of trial and at this stage it cannot be looked into by this court.

She goes on to submit that in the FIR, statement under section 161, 164 of Cr.P.C.,
prosecutrix has not stated that some one else has committed the intercourse with her hence at this stage it cannot be said that some one else has committed the crime.
The veracity of the statement of prosecutrix can be looked into by the trial court at the time of decision making of the case.
Any finding in this regard would influence the trial.
5. On 13.01.2023 victim and her parents appeared through Video Conferencing from the concerned DLSA and raised 'Serious Objection' with regard to grant of bail to the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions made herein above and also perused the case diary.
7. From the evidence collected by the prosecution prima facie prosecutrix appears to be less than 18 years.
Though in her cross examination she has stated that she got pregnant by some one else but the in the question by the trial court she has clarified this fact.
Therefore at this stage it would not be safe to come to a conclusion with regard to the credibility of the statement of the prosecutrix.

After careful examination of the material collected by the prosecution and giving thoughtful consideration on the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, this court does not find any good grounds to allow this bail application.
Thus the bail application is dismissed.

8. It is made clear that the observation made herein above is only for the purpose of decision making of the bail application of the applicant and to appreciate the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties.
It will not have any bearing on the merits of the case.
The learned trial court will decide the case on it own merits without being influenced by any observation made herein above.
Looking to the detention period it is expected that the learned trial court will expedite the trial.
9. Certified copy as per rule.
